title: Choose Sylph's visual world
question: Which world should define the Workspace where developers and agents build, preview, and test products together?

options.label: Prompt Desk
options.lineage: stage manager prompt books and live production desks
options.thesis: The product is on stage; Sylph is the disciplined desk that coordinates every cue around it.
options.viewport: A narrow Workspace ledger advances at left, a continuous agent prompt book occupies the center, and the live browser stage dominates the right with code and test evidence sliding up as cue sheets below it.
options.risk: The theatrical lineage becomes costume if labels stop being literal engineering language.

raised.raise: Every run and status change is visible at its exact point of consequence.
Color stays confined to a narrow band of live signals.
The active Workspace physically advances while the others remain legible.
Focus quiets adjacent regions without deleting their context.

options.label: Flight Strip Bay
options.lineage: air-traffic flight progress strips and coordination bays
options.thesis: Every Workspace is a live movement with ownership, destination, current state, and an unbroken handoff trail.
options.viewport: A compact strip bay on the left opens the selected Workspace into a wide center conversation and evidence log, while the browser preview owns a tall clear field on the right.
options.risk: It is the clearest operational metaphor and therefore the direction most likely to feel familiar.

options.label: Editable Stack
options.thesis: Browsing and authoring are two modes of the same Workspace object, never separate tools.
options.viewport: A black-and-white stack places the active product card large at center, with file, agent, browser, and skill cards linked through direct hand-painted controls.
options.case: It identifies strongly with software makers and unifies browsing with editing, but fixed cards weaken simultaneous preview context.
options.risk: Pixel nostalgia can overpower the modern remote Workspace if the stack feels imitative.

options.label: Workspace Lines
options.thesis: Workspaces are routes through intent, change, test, preview, and release; transfers reveal exactly where attention is needed.
options.viewport: The selected Workspace corridor runs across the top as a compact state line, feeding a centered work surface and a large live browser interchange on the right.
options.case: It makes parallel progress and transitions exceptionally clear, but its passenger-wayfinding lineage identifies less directly with software making.
options.risk: Too many colored routes can turn product state into decorative topology.

options.label: Instrument Counter
options.thesis: Agent runs and product state become physical readings on a calibrated bench.
options.viewport: A calibrated workbench surrounds the active preview with run, test, and change readings.
options.case: It overweights metrics and ornament relative to building the product.
options.kept: Every state change becomes visible at its exact point of consequence.
options.risk: The machinery can make ordinary product work feel performatively technical.

options.label: Signal Fringe
options.thesis: A mostly neutral workspace reveals live state through narrow spectral edges.
options.viewport: A wide white work surface lets agent activity and browser control appear as thin spectral boundaries.
options.case: Its evidence-analysis model does not map cleanly to routine software work.
options.kept: Color is reserved for a narrow band of live signals.
options.risk: The restraint can become generic productivity minimalism.

options.label: Workspace Archive
options.thesis: Each Workspace pulls forward from a compact indexed wall and opens to reveal its living contents.
options.viewport: A selected Workspace slides forward from a dense left wall and opens into the main work surface.
options.case: The catalog metaphor makes live Workspaces feel like stored inventory.
options.kept: The active Workspace advances physically while its neighbors remain visible.
options.risk: Object theatrics can overwhelm frequent navigation.

options.label: Focus Wall
options.thesis: The selected surface expands while every adjacent context yields without vanishing.
options.viewport: Rows of Workspace facets give way to an expanded browser and agent surface on focus.
options.case: Poster rails obscure code, causality, and review.
options.kept: Focus quiets surrounding regions without deleting their context.
options.risk: It can feel like content browsing instead of product building.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A refined dark agent IDE with a file tree, central editor, chat rail, and browser tab.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional resizable three-pane IDE keeps files left, code and preview center, and agent chat right.
canonCard.risk: It is immediately legible and indistinguishable from the category by design.
